What the weave does

Five decisions, made at the mill, that you feel on the couch.

01 / 05 Zero polyester

Mill sample card2/2 twill · lot 26-114

01 01 — Fiber

Nothing synthetic against your skin.

80% mulesing-free merino, 20% GOTS organic cotton. No microplastic shed in your living room, no static snap when you pull it over your shoulders, no petroleum sheen pretending to be softness.

FASERGEHALT: 80% WV / 20% CO · KEIN POLYESTER

02 02 — Climate

Cool in a laptop-warmed room.

Merino fiber buffers moisture vapor before it ever feels damp, so the blanket adapts as the room does — radiator on, window open, MacBook exhaling on your knees. Polyester traps that heat. Wool negotiates with it.

ATMUNGSAKTIV · TEMPERATURAUSGLEICHEND

03 03 — Provenance

Woven slow. About four yards an hour.

Every Decke 01 comes off the looms at Weberei Brandt, a third-generation family mill in Germany's Bavarian Alps, then gets raised once with natural teasel heads — the same finishing pass the mill has used since 1897. Dense 2/2 twill, 480 g/m², numbered on the selvedge before it leaves the valley.

GEWEBT IM ALLGÄU · SEIT 1897

04 04 — Health

Tested for what isn't there.

OEKO-TEX® Standard 100, Class I — the grade written for infant textiles. Undyed or plant-dyed colorways. No formaldehyde finish, no optical brighteners, no flame-retardant coating quietly off-gassing beside your face.

SCHADSTOFFGEPRÜFT · KLASSE I

05 05 — Nervous system

Three pounds of all-clear.

The dense twill drapes with a gentle, even pressure your body reads as “nothing is on fire.” Calm without the twenty-pound glass-bead furnace of a weighted blanket — you can actually fall asleep under this one in July.

3.1 LB (1,4 KG) · 55 × 79 IN

Read the label

Everything a blanket should have to declare, sewn in.

The sewn-in label is the one piece of honest documentation in the textile industry. Ours reads the way a spec sheet should: short, verifiable, and with nothing to hide behind a ™.

The shutdown ritual

Your calendar ends at six. Your cortisol doesn't. Give it a cue.

6:02 PM

Laptop lid down. Not sleep — down.

6:04 PM

Status set to away. Kettle on. Phone face-down on the shelf, not the armrest.

6:06 PM

Wool over the shoulders. The weight lands, the day ends. Feierabend.

2056

Someone who isn't born yet pulls it off the back of your couch and calls it theirs. Heirloom.

The arrival · Die Ankunft

The box is the overture. Nothing inside is filler.

Nº 1

The knot

Cotton twill wrap, tied by hand at the loom. There is no tape anywhere in the box. Your first act is untying a knot someone tied in Bavaria.

Handgebunden · Kein Plastik
Nº 2

The seal

Beeswax over the fold, pressed with the mill's 1897 stamp. It cracks once — and only for you.

Bienenwachs · Siegel der Weberei
Nº 3

The register card

Your blanket's number, your name, the weaver's initials — a duplicate of your line in the Webbuch, on card stock heavier than it needs to be. People frame these. We pretend to be surprised.

Aus dem Webbuch · Von Hand nummeriert
Nº 4

The blanket

Three pounds of teasel-raised twill, still carrying a trace of lanolin and the valley. Unfold it once and the box stops mattering.

Decke 01 · Zum Erben bestimmt

You will fold the wrap and keep it. Everyone does.
